one-line thesis: PNGS Reva delivered its first full standalone year with 70% revenue growth to INR439cr, driven by a 40% SSG in its 34 SIS stores and a strategic pivot to higher-margin natural diamonds. The key inflection is the rollout of 15 new EBOs funded by IPO proceeds, targeting a 25-30% CAGR while leveraging a unique 90% buyback policy to position natural diamonds as investable wealth against lab-grown substitutes.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR138cr (Q4, +139% YoY), INR439cr (FY26, +70% YoY vs restated FY25). EBITDA: INR31cr (Q4, 22% margin), INR95cr (FY26, 22% margin) - margin compression from 30%+ in restated period due to new standalone overheads (CEO, CFO, compliance, rent). PAT: INR21cr (Q4, +350%), INR65cr (FY26, +9%) - lower PAT growth due to higher depreciation/finance costs post-separation. Order Book: N/A (Retail). Net Debt: Utilized INR132-150cr of INR280cr total sanctions; strong cash position from INR380cr IPO. One-offs: ~INR55-60cr of FY26 revenue attributed to surplus gold trading (exchange consideration) rather than pure jewellery sales.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 25-30% CAGR for FY27/FY28. Margins: EBITDA 19-23% (absolute value growth prioritized over %); Gross Margin potential to expand from 28% to 30-35% as brand premium loads. Order Inflow: SSG expected 25-30% (base case) to 40% (if gold prices rise). Capex: INR20-25cr per EBO; INR2cr marketing spend per store over 12-18 months.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Retail business model; growth visibility via 14 remaining EBOs to be opened over 24 months (6-7 in FY27, balance in FY28).
segment / subsidiary detail: SIS (34 stores): INR313cr revenue in FY26, 40% SSG, asset-light (pay 4% commission to parent), 1.31x inventory turn. EBO (2 stores): Target INR9cr revenue/store at maturity (0.75 turn Year 1 -> 1.25-1.5x turn Year 3-4), EBITDA INR1.5cr (initial) to INR3.5-4cr (mature). Product Mix: Entry (15k-35k), Everyday (35k-1.5L), Occasion (1.5L-5L), Premium (5L-25L).
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion from 36 to 50+ stores by FY28; Geographic diversification (40% of new stores outside Maharashtra); Margin expansion via brand pricing power (currently priced like family jeweller); Working capital efficiency as backend inventory % drops from 15-20% to 12-15% with scale.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin 28% (FY26); EBITDA Margin 22%. Cost structure: Rent INR6L/month (EBO), Staff INR3.5L, Ops INR2L. Marketing spend guided at 3-4% of sales. Margins pressured by standalone overheads but expected to recover as brand premium is added to diamond pricing.
capex / expansion: Asset-light model (leased properties only). INR20-25cr per EBO setup. INR287cr IPO proceeds earmarked for expansion/working capital; INR35cr for marketing. No property purchase planned.
capital allocation: IPO proceeds (INR380cr) deployed for 15 new stores and marketing. No equity dilution planned for next 2 years; growth funded by internal accruals (INR64cr added to reserves in FY26) and unused debt headroom (INR150-200cr available).
risks & watch-items: Gold price volatility impacting consumer demand (though management sees inelasticity for weddings); Inventory turnover dilution from new EBO ramp-up; Competition from lab-grown diamonds (mitigated by no-resale-value narrative); Execution risk in expanding outside Maharashtra (longer breakeven: 18-24 months).
management quality / tone: Confident and pragmatic; emphasizes 'absolute value' over margin percentages; strong conviction in natural diamond wealth narrative; transparent about margin compression due to separation costs; conservative on guidance (25-30% vs 40% prior).
non-obvious takeaways: ~12-14% of reported revenue (INR55-60cr) is from trading surplus gold received as exchange consideration, not core jewellery margin; the 90% buyback policy effectively creates a put option for customers, differentiating natural diamonds as 'investable' vs lab-grown 'consumable'; sister concern Gargi targets lower karat (14k) and lower color (H/I) diamonds to avoid cannibalization.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rapid proliferation of lab-grown diamonds threatening traditional jewellery value proposition | PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery Ltd | beneficiary | High | Company's strict natural-only stance combined with a 90% buyback policy positions it as a hedge against lab-grown depreciation; explicitly markets natural diamonds as inheritable wealth, capturing the premium segment unwilling to compromise on resale value. |
| High gold prices potentially suppressing discretionary jewellery demand | PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Management notes that high gold prices actually increased reported SSG (40%) due to value effects; their focus on absolute margin value rather than percentage protects earnings even if mix shifts to higher gold content. |
| Organized players gaining share from unorganized family jewellers | PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery Ltd | beneficiary | High | Leverages 190-year legacy of parent P.N. Gadgil & Sons to capture trust-deficit customers moving to organized sector; asset-light SIS model allows rapid penetration without heavy capex. |

hero.oneLiner: Retail-focused diamond jewellery brand 'Reva', carved out of Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons' 190+ year legacy via a January 2025 slump sale, selling diamond and precious-stone studded gold/platinum jewellery through 34 stores across western India.
hero.industry: Branded Natural Diamond Jewellery (Premium & Occasion Wear)

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Retail-focused diamond jewellery brand 'Reva', carved out of Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons' 190+ year legacy via a January 2025 slump sale, selling diamond and precious-stone studded gold/platinum jewellery through 34 stores across western India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery Limited retails a wide range of jewellery made using diamonds and precious/semi-precious stones studded into gold and platinum, plus plain platinum jewellery (rings, bracelets, chains), under its flagship brand 'Reva'. As of the RHP it operates 34 Stores across 25 cities in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka (647.15 Running Feet) under FOCO, FOFO and one COCO format, largely as shop-in-shop spaces inside Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited's retail stores under a Franchise Agreement dated February 1, 2025 (amended June 26, 2025). The company does not manufacture in-house, has no e-commerce platform, and does not source products internationally; ornaments accounted for 99.6-99.75% of total income across FY23-FY25 and H1 FY26.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited — Corporate Promoter: Transferred the diamond business to the Company via slump-sale Business Transfer Agreement dated January 31, 2025 (net assets ₹1,623.01 million; consideration ₹1,62,30,09,000; common-control Ind AS 103 accounting from April 1, 2022, no independent valuation legally required). Under the Franchise Agreement (February 1, 2025, amended June 26, 2025) it provides retail space, logistics, electricity, furniture, security and billing software; 32 of 33 promoter retail locations host the Company's shop-in-shop stores, and in FOFO mall stores inventory is transferred to and billed by the Corporate Promoter.
- PNGS Gargi Fashion Jewellery Limited — Group Company: Identified as the Group Company under the Materiality Policy (related-party transactions); shares common directors with the Company.
- Puneet Shares and Finance Private Limited — Promoter Group entity (common directorships): Govind Vishwanath Gadgil and Amit Yeshwant Modak hold directorships.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: SIS (34 stores): INR313cr revenue in FY26, 40% SSG, asset-light (pay 4% commission to parent), 1.31x inventory turn. EBO (2 stores): Target INR9cr revenue/store at maturity (0.75 turn Year 1 -> 1.25-1.5x turn Year 3-4), EBITDA INR1.5cr (initial) to INR3.5-4cr (mature). Product Mix: Entry (15k-35k), Everyday (35k-1.5L), Occasion (1.5L-5L), Premium (5L-25L).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Ornaments (diamond studded jewellery including precious stones):** Rings, Mangalsutra, Earrings, Necklaces, Bangles, Bracelets, Chains, Nose pins, Pendants, Precious stones, Others (loose diamonds, fusion bars, loose gemstones, bespoke orders, direct office sales)
- **Gold:** Sale of excess gold from customer gold exchange (from H1 FY26; 14.12% of H1 FY26 revenue)
- **Platinum:** Plain platinum jewellery - rings, bracelets, chains

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Retail jewellery consumers - Maharashtra (97.54% of H1 FY26 revenue; 96.97% FY25)
- Karnataka (1.55% of H1 FY26 revenue)
- Gujarat (0.91% of H1 FY26 revenue)
- No online/e-commerce sales and no exports in FY23-FY25 or H1 FY26

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: No backward integration: the Company does not manufacture any products in-house (no revenue from manufacturing activities in FY23–FY25 and H1 FY26). It acquires finished diamond and gemstone-studded jewellery directly from various third-party manufacturing partners and Karigars in India — sourcing is limited to finished products from domestic manufacturing partners; no direct import/export of raw materials such as diamonds, gemstones or precious metals, except customer-provided gold for specific design orders. Purchases of stock-in-trade from manufacturing partners: ₹1,392.64 mn (70.04% of revenue from operations) in FY23, ₹1,663.63 mn (85.04%) in FY24, ₹1,971.41 mn (76.36%) in FY25 and ₹2,485.72 mn (158.61%) in H1 FY26. Design is partly in-house (dual design approach: in-house design studio staffed with 2 designers as of September 30, 2025, plus curated selections and joint design initiatives with third-party manufacturers). Forward/retail infrastructure is leveraged from Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited under a Franchise Agreement dated February 1, 2025 (amended June 26, 2025) — retail space, logistics, electricity, furniture, security and billing software; under the FOFO model inventory is transferred to the Corporate Promoter, which retails the products under the Reva brand. The diamond business itself was acquired from the Corporate Promoter via a slump-sale Business Transfer Agreement dated January 31, 2025 (inventory ₹1,627.67 mn and gratuity liability ₹4.67 mn transferred; net value ₹1,623.01 mn; lump-sum consideration ₹1,62,30,09,000). Quality control practices across the value chain include specialised tools for assessing clarity, cut, colour, carat weight and metal purity, and regular supply-chain audits. Concentrated regional footprint enables centralised inventory management, distribution and optimised transport routes through its logistics service provider.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A - Retail business model; growth visibility via 14 remaining EBOs to be opened over 24 months (6-7 in FY27, balance in FY28).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 25-30% CAGR for FY27/FY28. Margins: EBITDA 19-23% (absolute value growth prioritized over %); Gross Margin potential to expand from 28% to 30-35% as brand premium loads. Order Inflow: SSG expected 25-30% (base case) to 40% (if gold prices rise). Capex: INR20-25cr per EBO; INR2cr marketing spend per store over 12-18 months.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion from 36 to 50+ stores by FY28; Geographic diversification (40% of new stores outside Maharashtra); Margin expansion via brand pricing power (currently priced like family jeweller); Working capital efficiency as backend inventory % drops from 15-20% to 12-15% with scale.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Gross margin stable across store formats: FOCO 26.62%, FOFO 27.14%, COCO 26.67% in H1 FY26 (blended 26.67%)
- Revenue mix dominated by wedding-linked categories - rings (20.8-27.2%) and mangalsutra (21.3-23.4%) across periods
- New gold revenue line from H1 FY26 (14.12% of revenue) from sale of excess exchanged gold after internal consumption
- Asset-light FOCO model (promoter owns/leases space, Company runs inventory and operations) keeps store capex low
- Heavy geographic concentration in Maharashtra (~97% of revenue) with small Gujarat/Karnataka contributions

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin 28% (FY26); EBITDA Margin 22%. Cost structure: Rent INR6L/month (EBO), Staff INR3.5L, Ops INR2L. Marketing spend guided at 3-4% of sales. Margins pressured by standalone overheads but expected to recover as brand premium is added to diamond pricing.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds (INR380cr) deployed for 15 new stores and marketing. No equity dilution planned for next 2 years; growth funded by internal accruals (INR64cr added to reserves in FY26) and unused debt headroom (INR150-200cr available).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company plans to expand from its current 34 largely promoter-hosted shop-in-shop Stores (one COCO store operational since September 4, 2025) to 15 brand-exclusive New Stores owned and operated by the Company by Fiscal 2028, focused on Tier-1 cities and selectively Tier-2 cities in Maharashtra and other metro cities in India. The rollout is the primary object of the Fresh Issue (up to ₹3,800 million): ₹2,865.64 million for setting up the New Stores (deployed ₹243.14m / ₹1,641.05m / ₹981.46m over three fiscals) plus ₹354.00 million of launch marketing, shifting the model from FOCO/FOFO dependence on the Corporate Promoter toward standalone brand-exclusive retail.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and pragmatic; emphasizes 'absolute value' over margin percentages; strong conviction in natural diamond wealth narrative; transparent about margin compression due to separation costs; conservative on guidance (25-30% vs 40% prior).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Flagship 'Reva' brand carries the 190+ year legacy of Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited
- Asset-light FOCO shop-in-shop model minimises capital expenditure on standalone stores while maximising visibility in high-traffic retail environments
- Leverages Corporate Promoter's established infrastructure and customer footfall while maintaining distinct brand identity
- Design-led brand offering customizable diamond jewellery across price points, occasions and customer preferences
- Consistent gross margins across store models (~26.6%-27.1% in H1 FY26)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Gold price volatility impacting consumer demand (though management sees inelasticity for weddings); Inventory turnover dilution from new EBO ramp-up; Competition from lab-grown diamonds (mitigated by no-resale-value narrative); Execution risk in expanding outside Maharashtra (longer breakeven: 18-24 months).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: ~12-14% of reported revenue (INR55-60cr) is from trading surplus gold received as exchange consideration, not core jewellery margin; the 90% buyback policy effectively creates a put option for customers, differentiating natural diamonds as 'investable' vs lab-grown 'consumable'; sister concern Gargi targets lower karat (14k) and lower color (H/I) diamonds to avoid cannibalization.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up 15 brand-exclusive company-owned-and-operated New Stores under the 'Reva' brand by Fiscal 2028.**
- **Deploy ₹2,865.64 million of Net Proceeds towards setting up the 15 New Stores, phased ₹243.14 million / ₹1,641.05 million / ₹981.46 million across three fiscals.**
- **Spend ₹354.00 million on marketing and promotional expenses for the launch of the 15 New Stores to enhance local awareness and visibility of the 'Reva' brand (phased ₹23.60m / ₹212.40m / ₹118.00m).**
- **Focus New Store rollout on Tier-1 cities while selectively exploring Tier-2 cities in Maharashtra and other metro cities in India.**
- **Amount utilised for general corporate purposes shall not exceed 25% of the Gross Proceeds of the up-to-₹3,800 million Fresh Issue.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand footprint to 15 brand-exclusive company-owned-and-operated (COCO) New Stores under the 'Reva' brand by Fiscal 2028
- Target Tier-1 cities and selectively explore Tier-2 cities in Maharashtra and other metro cities in India for New Stores
- Invest in marketing and promotion around New Store launches to enhance local brand awareness and visibility of 'Reva'
- Operate as an independent diamond-jewellery player post carve-out, building a distinct market identity from the Corporate Promoter

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Corporate history] The company is stated to be "Formerly known as Gadgil Metals & Commoditie[s]", CIN L32111PN2024PLC236494, registered at Abhiruchi Mall, Wadgaon Budruk, Sinhagad Road, Pune; the FY26 cash flow statement carries a line "Less: Net cash and cash equivalents generated for diamond business not taken over" of Rs 34 Mn in Mar-25 and 0 in Mar-26.
- [Governance] Board comprises Govind Gadgil (Chairman & Non-Executive Director, 5th generation promoter), Amit Modak (WTD & CEO, 40+ years including 27 with the PNG Group and 13 as CEO of P N Gadgil & Sons) and Aditya Modak (Non-Executive Director), with independent directors Ranjeet Natu, Aparna Purohit and Ravindra Lale; CFO Kisan Shendkar (18+ years), COO Vrujendra Waghchaure (24+ years), CS Kirti Vaidya (9+ years). Leadership team stated to bring 85+ years of combined experience.
- [Industry] Deck cites (Care Edge, Nov'25) the Indian G&J industry at Rs 8,809 Bn in CY24, growing at a 10.6% CAGR since CY20 and projected at an 11.7% CAGR till CY29; India produces over 90% of the world's polished diamonds; gross margins by type in CY24(E) shown as gold 40-50%, diamond 30-40% and other 10-20%.
- [Industry] India diamond market size shown as Rs 457 Bn (CY20), 590 (CY21), 623 (CY22), 586 (CY23), 596 (CY24E), 616 (CY25P), 631 (CY26P), 647 (CY27P), 666 (CY28P) and 686 Bn (CY29P).
- [Demand driver] Deck attributes part of its own demand to rising gold prices causing a shift from gold jewellery to diamond jewellery, stating this shift has been seen across its stores in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka.
